summary: Your reef-monitoring mission is well argued and clearly structured. You name users and needs, justify an STK-based plan with contingencies and sources, and your orbit calculations correctly expose a coverage shortfall. To reach the top of the Accomplished band, show the inclination working, quantify the revisit shortfall, derive requirement values, and fix the [6] citation and Gantt Week 10 inconsistency.
next_steps: In Preliminary Progress, add the J2 nodal-precession calculation that yields the 97.8° sun-synchronous inclination, so the key orbit assumption can be checked.
Quantify the coverage shortfall: count required swaths/passes versus daylight passes per week to show explicitly why weekly revisit fails, rather than concluding qualitatively.

Reconcile the Gantt (Image 1) with the text: STK Simulations runs to Week 10 while the text says design and simulation finish by Week 9; also replace reference [6] with a BoM sea-surface-temperature source.

criteria.C1: You give a clear goal, four numbered objectives and named users (AIMS, GBRMPA) with distinct needs, grounded in bleaching evidence and cited literature. To secure full marks, derive the 10 m GSD, weekly revisit and 24 h delivery values from your sources or a sensor trade, rather than asserting them, and tie each requirement explicitly back to the user need it serves.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt (Figure 1) has dated weeks, per-task descriptions and mission-driven sequencing, plus a risk/contingency table with triggers and a source table; STK is justified against mission questions. For full marks, align the Gantt with your text: the STK Simulations bar runs to Week 10 although you state design and simulation finish by Week 9. Clarify whether Week 10 is float only.
criteria.C3: Your hand calculations for a, T, orbits/day, SSO inclination, ground-track shift and swath are numerically correct and interpreted, and they honestly expose a coverage shortfall that feeds your contingency plan. To reach full marks, show the J2 nodal-precession working behind the 97.8° inclination, and quantify the revisit failure by counting required swaths/passes against daylight passes per week rather than concluding qualitatively.
criteria.C4: The report is logically structured with clear headings, readable prose, labelled Figure 1 and Tables 2–3, consistent formatting, and in-text citations that match the reference list. For full marks, correct reference [6]: it is a NOAA climate-change page cited for BoM sea-surface-temperature products, so add the actual BoM source. Consider replacing news article [4] with the primary method source.
